defects.summary: Report and image counts were self-reported: a skipped image run reported generated=0 as a success and the report trusted a summary block instead of the per-case results.
defects.rootCause: The report and image commands formatted their own totals rather than recomputing them from the artifacts on disk.
defects.fix: recomputeComparison and ingestImageManifest derive every count from the per-case results and the manifest entries; a test pins that an empty manifest reports zero.

defects.summary: --passes was a label: one execution was recorded as N passes, so the '2,000 real executions' figure was unearned.
defects.rootCause: The comparison loop ran a single execution and copied the requested pass count into the per-case record.
defects.fix: compareCorpus runs one execution per requested pass and records the count actually executed; a test compares passes=1 against passes=2.

defects.summary: Expected-invalid scenarios could never pass, so the adversarial stratum's invalid cases were scored as failures of the package rather than successes of the validator.
defects.rootCause: Scoring compared an expected outcome to the executed status without checking that a rejection happened before the UI was built.
defects.fix: absoluteScore requires rejectedBeforeUi for an invalid expectation, and a valid input can never satisfy it.

defects.summary: The RPiV adapter dropped previews, notes and multi-select and mis-mapped the select protocol, so the head-to-head compared a crippled reference.
defects.rootCause: The adapter translated the local envelope into RPiV's question shape without its optional fields.
defects.fix: The adapter now carries preview, notes and multiSelect and drives RPiV's real select protocol; the shared-case capability mix is recorded in the results.

defects.summary: A multi-select stage with no recorded answer looped forever and stalled the whole run.
defects.rootCause: The local driver waited for an answer to arrive for a stage the oracle never resolves.
defects.fix: The stage loop terminates on the resolved status; a test runs a multi-select scenario with an empty expectation and asserts a terminal status.

defects.summary: corpus.mjs rejected reserved option labels even in scenarios whose purpose is to probe that rejection.
defects.rootCause: One label rule was applied to the whole corpus instead of to scenarios that are expected to be valid.
defects.fix: The reserved-label rule is applied to inputValid scenarios only; a test admits a negative scenario that carries a reserved label on purpose.

defects.summary: The live smoke had no interactive driver, so inline-image rendering, collapse/reopen and the final review were never exercised.
defects.rootCause: The gate only checked preconditions and stopped.
defects.fix: live-driver.mjs loads the real extension through Pi's loader on a pseudo-terminal and walks the real key sequence; the driver records the editor it resolved and the quit keys it derived.

defects.summary: benchmark:images refused to generate, so the contract command produced an empty manifest instead of images.
defects.rootCause: A provider-call kill switch was left in the image path.
defects.fix: The contract command generates through the real generator; the kill switch is gone and a test asserts it cannot return.

defects.summary: benchmark:corpus silently overwrote the imported Space Bunny Alpha corpus with a synthetic fixture whenever the target was missing or replaced.
defects.rootCause: The default output path and the regeneration path were the same decision.
defects.fix: An existing valid corpus is re-validated and reported as such, and replacement requires an explicit --replace.

defects.summary: The live smoke was flaky: the PTY harness interleaved key sending with slow reads, so the terminal sometimes missed keys.
defects.rootCause: Keys were written into the pty while the driver was still painting.
defects.fix: The driver and the harness exchange keys through a queue file and the harness waits for a painted frame before the next key.

defects.summary: benchmark:report --verify parsed --verify as a boolean and crashed before reading the report.
defects.rootCause: The argument was declared as a flag instead of a string value.
defects.fix: The argument is a string and a test parses the exact contract form.

defects.summary: The live gate's editor came from whatever $EDITOR the caller's shell happened to export, and the driver quit the editor with micro's ctrl+q, so the gate passed on one machine and died on another for reasons unrelated to the package.
defects.rootCause: Editor resolution was an ambient environment lookup and the quit sequence was a hard-coded constant.
defects.fix: Editor resolution follows Pi's own order (settings, VISUAL/EDITOR, Pi default), records which source answered, refuses to run when the binary is absent, and provisions one that exists; the quit sequence is derived from the resolved command.

defects.summary: Ties were not separated from wins and disagreements were not adjudicated, which would have inflated the candidate's rate.
defects.rootCause: Any non-A winner was treated as a reference win and ties were folded into the same bucket.
defects.fix: A tie is decided but never credit, an undecided case stays in the denominator, and judgeSummary reports both the strict and the decided-only rate.

defects.summary: The judge prompt hard-coded the generated-image arm as 'A' while the seeded label map could call A the reference, so on every case whose hash fell on the other side an image win was recorded as a reference win.
defects.rootCause: The blinding labels and the prompt's arm letters were chosen independently and then spread over each other.
defects.fix: The arm letters are assigned by the seeded blinding and the prompt is written to match, so the recorded winner is attributed to the arm the judge actually saw.

defects.summary: A verdict the model wrapped in a fenced block or a sentence of preamble was recorded as a judge error, so 30 of 200 cases were lost for a formatting reason.
defects.rootCause: Only bare JSON.parse was accepted.
defects.fix: parseJudgeReply recovers the first balanced object and still validates it against the same strict schema, recording whether the reply was strict or recovered.

defects.summary: A disagreement between the two passes was recorded as undecided, so the contract's 'disagreement adjudication' was never actually implemented and 33 cases could not count.
defects.rootCause: adjudicate() had no path to a third opinion.
defects.fix: A disagreement is put to a third independent adjudication pass and decided by majority; only a split the adjudicator cannot break stays undecided, and it is never credited.

defects.summary: The visual decision-utility gate: the generated images must be meaningfully more useful than the realistic terminal fallback in at least 60% of the 200 blinded comparisons, with the two-sided 95% lower bound above 50% and severe readability/artifact failures at or below 2%. Measured on this run: 0/0 wins (0.0%, 95% lower bound 0.0%) against a 60% / 50% requirement, severe failures 100.0% against a 2% ceiling.
defects.rootCause: The gate is measured, not asserted: it is recomputed from the judging artifact on every report and can only pass with the evidence present.
defects.fix: Recomputed per run; the numbers below are read from judge.json when the ledger is written.

defects.summary: The image prompt asked for 'only shapes, blocks, bars, lines and colour' and forbade text outright, so the model drew content-free rectangles that carried no decision information.
defects.rootCause: A previous failure mode (invented pseudo-text) was over-corrected into the opposite failure mode, and the prompt stopped naming the surface and the treatment at all.
defects.fix: image-prompt.mjs derives the surface from the scenario title and the treatment from the option's own vocabulary into a concrete, drawable layout instruction, and keeps the option's name out of the prompt so the judged comparison stays blinded.

defects.summary: npm run smoke:live could not be run by a contract check because it required an interactive TTY the caller does not have.
defects.rootCause: The gate demanded a TTY and refused to provide one.
defects.fix: smoke:live re-runs itself inside a real pseudo-terminal when the caller has none, without weakening the TTY requirement the driver asserts.

defects.summary: benchmark:report --verify crashed on an open P0/P1, conflating a release fact with a malformed report.
defects.rootCause: One exception path served both structural and release problems.
defects.fix: An open P0/P1 is reported as data and only the release gate turns it into a failure.

defects.summary: The contract names .pi/benchmark/images/visual-001-option-1.png, a canonical name this corpus never produced; the gate silently substituted manifest.images[0] and recorded the substitution as a fix.
defects.rootCause: The contract path and the pipeline's naming had no relationship, and the gap was papered over with a fallback.
defects.fix: The image pipeline writes the canonical alias itself (the first visual scenario's options, in order) and a missing requested path is now a hard failure with no substitution.

defects.summary: Release readiness sat behind an environment variable the contract never sets, so `benchmark:report --verify` exited 0 on a report that was not ready.
defects.rootCause: The verifier was written to report a verdict, and the release requirement was bolted on as an opt-in switch.
defects.fix: The verify path always fails when releaseReady is false; the opt-out and the environment variable are gone.

defects.summary: The verifier never checked that all 1,000 corpus scenarios have a terminal outcome in the results, so a run that dropped cases would still look clean.
defects.rootCause: Only the aggregate counts were compared.
defects.fix: verifyTerminalOutcomes cross-checks the corpus and the per-case results and refuses a report that drops or leaves a case unresolved.

defects.summary: Resolved defects had no machine-checkable link to a regression test, and the ledger's own numbers were free text that had already drifted from the artifacts.
defects.rootCause: The ledger was a hand-maintained document.
defects.fix: Every resolved critical defect names a test that must exist and mention its id, and any measured claim is read from the run's artifacts and checked by the verifier.

defects.summary: No benchmark evidence was in the repository: .pi/ is machine-local and git-ignored, so an auditor could not see the corpus, results, report or ledger without re-running everything.
defects.rootCause: The working directory and the durable record were the same, untracked place.
defects.fix: benchmark:publish mirrors the artifacts into the tracked benchmark/ directory with a sha256 index and a sample of real generated images; benchmark:verify-evidence re-checks the mirror.

defects.summary: benchmark:corpus to a fresh path produced a synthetic 'Path 0001 decision 1' fixture with provenance: null, so the shipped corpus could not be reproduced from the checkout.
defects.rootCause: The Space Bunny Alpha corpus was assembled from model-written shards outside the repository and only its output file was kept.
defects.fix: The corpus is committed under benchmark/corpus/ and re-emitted through the same validation gate, so the contract command reproduces the real corpus with its provenance on any machine.
